claim: Every globally minimum original-current-edge AF cutset avoids edges strictly inside every common proper pendant subtree of the two current forests.
scope: Exact finite binary rooted forests, actual current AF minimum; source/current compatibility explicit. Not forced-extension minima.
reason_to_test: Reviewed root-safe normalization with minimum-fragment survival appears to imply this by applying it with E2 empty to the two common child subtrees at each internal node. It would sharpen nonempty-fragment survival to intactness and help the contraction interface.
negative_control: The same statement for arbitrary AF cutsets is false: singleton-producing leaf cuts include common-subtree internal edges.
acceptance: Finite checks are candidate evidence only. An exact corollary proof and fresh review are required before using intactness as a forest theorem.
